messages.subject: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed()
parts:
Dear Professor Rue and R-INLA groups,

I have run different survival models survival models using R-INLA and faced the following errors

1. The coxPH model has not given the output (it stopped generating the results after some iteration)
2. In the Weibull parametric model, I got the Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed(). In fact, I have included the verbose=TRUE as well.

Kindly see the code below and let you suggest to me what to do. 

formula=inla.surv(mydata$time,mydata$Status)~Region+Residence+Mother_education+Source_of_water+Family_size+Toilet_type+

Age_of_mother_at_first_birth+Wealth_index+Marital_status+Mother_occupation+Birth_type+Sex_of_child+BORD+Place_of_delivery+f(clus,model="iid")

model1=inla(formula,family="coxph",data=mydata,verbose=T,control.hazard=list(model="rw1",n.intervals=20),debug=FALSE,control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,waic=TRUE))

summary(model1)

 

formula1=inla.surv(time,Status)~Region+Residence+Mother_education+Source_of_water+Family_size+Toilet_type+Age_of_mother_at_first_birth+Wealth_index+Marital_status+Mother_occupation+Birth_type+Sex_of_child+BORD+Place_of_delivery+f(clus,model="iid",hyper=list(prec=list(param=c(0.001,0.001))))

 

model2=inla(formula1,family="weibullsurv",data=mydata,verbose=TRUE,control.compute=list(dic=TRUE,waic=TRUE))

 

summary(model2)

 

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :

  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.

  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

--

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed()
parts:
Hi,

there are several things here. I modified the code, and I didn't do them
all.

for the coxph, I guess you'll run out of memory. I did on my laptop, and
I ran in on our server. you can reduce the ammount by reducing the
number of nodes in the baseline hazard, and number of threads in the
computations (argument num.threads) you have to see what you make work.
you can also add control.inla=list(int.strategy='eb') which will help (a
lot).

for the weibull, you had several observations that were exactly 0, and
this cause a problem. I added small noise for those, as you see, and its
fine then.

I guess your $Status is 1 and 2, and this is what you want? see
?inla.surv normally, its 0 or 1, not 1 and 2, [different cencoring...].
please check.

there were also an issue with using improper prior for the intercept, so
I added prec=1 for the intercept and the fixed effects.

and better priors... Gamma(eps,eps) prior is very bad [I know, it have
been used a lot].

Hopefully, this will allow you to get started...

Best
H
